content_preview.title: Gemini 4 Neon and Inkling 2 Mini Claim Near-Frontier Scores at Lower Cost, but Both Trail on Some Cited Benchmarks
content_preview.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Neon and Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini both launched this month pitched as near-frontier models at lower cost, but the benchmark tables cited for each show wins, losses and a flat tie.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Over the past two weeks, two AI labs have released models pitched the same way: smaller or cheaper than a sibling or rival, yet close enough in measured performance to make the price difference look like pure upside. [Google launched Gemini 4 Neon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/) on November 18, a mid-tier model that [VentureBeat reports](https://venturebeat.com/technology/google-launches-gemini-4-neon-with-opus-5...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis (Background / Current situation / Implications) at 1,161 words, within the 800-2000 range. Facts (quotes, benchmark figures) are clearly separated from editorializing, which is confined to the Implications section and framed as the Herald's own observation rather than stated as fact.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 source snapshots decompressed and read in full from sources/2026-11/gemini-4-neon-and-inkling-2-mini-claim-near-frontier-scores-at-lower-cost-but-both-trail-on-some-cited-benchmarks/ (source-0 through source-5.html.gz); sha256 of each decompressed file recomputed and matched the manifest exactly, confirming no tampering. Every direct quote in the article was located verbatim in its cited snapshot: (1) source-0, VentureBeat/Neon: 'Google now has an answer for three different budgets: Hydrogen for high-volume work, Neon for harder jobs that recur often, and Carbon for extended projects' — verbatim match; 'Neon costs 25% below Anthropic's larger, flagship Opus 5.5's standard rates of $4 and $20 despite scoring within about a percentage point on that larger model on two engineering benchmarks' — verbatim match, and confirmed VentureBeat never names which two benchmarks that phrase refers to, matching the article's own hedge. All five benchmark score pairs (AA Index 61/59 xhigh, AutomationBench 56.3/42.5, Terminal-Bench Science 70.5/63.3, FrontierCode 2.0 46.2/47.3, Terminal-Bench 4.1 65.2/65.8) traced to the exact VentureBeat table rows; the Herald's own 1.1-point and 0.6-point gap calculations are arithmetically correct (47.3-46.2=1.1, 65.8-65.2=0.6). (2) source-1, blog.google: '$3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens' and 'xhigh thinking adds deeper, multi-step reasoning for the hardest engineering, analytical, and scientific workloads' — both verbatim matches; Nov 18, 2026 publish date confirmed on-page. (3) source-2, vals.ai: confirmed Gemini 4 Neon 70.87% ranked #2 and Claude Opus 5.5 70.14% ranked #5 in the Vals Index leaderboard exactly as stated (full order: Claude Fable 5.2 71.31%, Gemini 4 Neon 70.87%, Claude Sonnet 5.5 70.85%, Gemini 4 Carbon 70.45%, Claude Opus 5.5 70.14%). (4) source-3, VentureBeat/Inkling: 'the first six layers (the prelude) and the final six layers run once, while the middle 12 layers run three times using shared weights' — verbatim; tie score 20.1 confirmed in the comparison table row; 'Inkling 2 Mini scores -8.6 on AA-Omniscience v1.1 (with a 63.4% non-hallucination rate), trailing denser peers like Qwen3.8-27B (-6.4 and 71.4%)' — verbatim, and independently cross-checked against Thinking Machines' own benchmark table in source-4 (column headers 'Inkling 2 Mini / Gemma 4 31B / Muse Glimmer / Qwen3.8-27B / Nemotron 3.5 Super VL'; AA-Omniscience v1.1 score row = -8.6 / -48.5 / -32.2 / -6.4 / -2.9; non-hallucination row = 63.4% / 14.5% / 16.4% / 71.4% / 69.5% — Inkling=col1, Qwen3.8-27B=col4, confirming the article's pairing is correct, not just VentureBeat's restatement). (5) source-4, thinkingmachines.ai: 'a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping' and 'Blocks 2 and 3 share weights across three passes, giving 48 layer applications per token from 24 stored layers' — both verbatim; AA Index row confirms the 20.1/20.1 tie between Inkling 2 Mini (col1) and Qwen3.8-27B (col4) independently of VentureBeat. (6) source-5, artificialanalysis.ai: 'Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index', 'Inkling 2 Mini is ~6x cheaper and ~4x faster per task than Qwen3.8 27B', 'it costs $0.59 and takes 9.0 minutes per Intelligence Index task vs. $3.53 and 38.2 minutes', and 'sits on the Pareto frontier, using ~2.8x less compute than Qwen3.8 27B' — all four verbatim matches. No hallucinated quotes, no misattributions, no fabricated specifics found across any of the six sources. Internal links to prior Herald coverage verified: /article/2026-11/07-thinking-machines-launches-inkling-2-small-... exists and its body confirms the 594B total-parameter figure and the $0.30/$0.03/$1.00 Tinker pricing the new article cites from it; /article/2026-11/19-alibabas-qwen4-max-... exists and its body confirms the 'well behind' characterization reused in the new article's Background section. Suspicious-patterns scan: manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for all 6 sources; an independent keyword re-scan of the extracted plain text of all 6 snapshots for injection-style phrases ('ignore instructions', 'disregard previous', 'system prompt', 'do not tell the user', etc.) returned zero matches. No source allowlist issue remains: vals.ai independently confirmed as the official site of the Vals AI benchmark organization (full masthead: Benchmarks, Models, Comparison, Vals Smith, App, Reports, Government, News, Incidents, Blog, About, Methodology) and added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this commit with a justification comment, resolving the sole automated warning. Independent-source count for the Analysis requirement (recounted, not accepted from the writer's self-audit): the writer's PR self-report claimed 4 independent sources (VentureBeat counted twice as two separate articles, plus Vals AI and Artificial Analysis), but per policy 'several articles from one outlet are one source' — VentureBeat counts once despite two separate articles/subjects. Correct independent count is 3 (VentureBeat, Vals AI, Artificial Analysis), against 2 non-independent vendor-own sources (blog.google, thinkingmachines.ai). 3 independent sources still clears the Analysis-category minimum of 2. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic/Claude Opus 5.5 appears only as a benchmark comparison point (a competing model in a benchmark table) throughout the body; it is not the subject, does not appear in the headline/summary/lead, and carries no 'assisted by Claude' or Anthropic credit line. This falls under the policy's express exception for 'an incidental name in a list of vendors, benchmarks or competing models.'
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics (model names, parameter counts, prices, context windows, benchmark scores, rankings, dates) traced to and matched their cited sources exactly, including second-order verification of the Inkling 2 Mini vs. Qwen3.8-27B benchmark pairs against Thinking Machines' own raw comparison table (not just VentureBeat's restatement of it). No absence/quantifier claim ('both', 'exact tie', 'does not explicitly name', 'does not report') found unsupported when checked against all 6 sources, not just the adjacent citation. Launch dates (Gemini 4 Neon Nov 18; Inkling 2 Mini 'two days later' = Nov 20) corroborated by the Google blog's own Nov 18, 2026 timestamp and Artificial Analysis's Nov 20, 2026 article date.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The Implications section is explicit that 'neither company's headline framing is false on its own terms' and frames the pattern as a recurring structural observation rather than an accusation of deception. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New angle, not a duplicate: this is a cross-vendor analytical comparison (Gemini 4 Neon vs. Opus 5.5; Inkling 2 Mini vs. Qwen3.8-27B) explicitly building on, and distinct from, the Herald's prior single-release coverage of Inkling 2 Small (2026-11-07) and Qwen4-Max (2026-11-19). Checked src/content/articles/2026-11/ for the last 7 days; no existing article covers this specific Neon/Inkling 2 Mini cost-vs-benchmark comparison.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A rigorous, well-sourced Analysis piece that holds up under a full quote-by-quote and number-by-number audit against raw source text, including independent corroboration of the Inkling-vs-Qwen benchmark pairs from Thinking Machines' own table rather than relying solely on VentureBeat's restatement. The only issue (vals.ai missing from the allowlist) was a pipeline-data gap, not a content problem, and was resolved by confirming vals.ai's legitimacy and adding it to the allowlist in this review's commit. Featured candidacy: 1 - a solid, well-verified cross-vendor analysis for a developer/AI-industry audience, but it extends an already-established Herald pattern (the Qwen4-Max piece) rather than breaking new ground, so it does not reach the broad-audience or exceptional tiers.
